thesis: Common ground is not a single phenomenon but the accidental convergence of at least two independently operating mechanisms: one tracking mutual public commitment, which licenses what can be presupposed in assertion, and another tracking mutual representation, which coordinates joint activity — conversation included — and licenses what can be insinuated (and otherwise conveyed off-record) within it.

outlines.title: Common Ground as Accidental Convergence
outlines.shape: Establish that two classes of conversational move are licensed by different conditions — one requiring public settlement, one requiring its absence — show the two come apart again at repair, argue from the inversion to independence, then show unified accounts cannot absorb both without idle structure.
outlines.structure_note: The negative case against unified accounts comes late (§8) rather than as a literature section, because the dilemma it poses is generated by the differentials and the transition datum and cannot be stated before them.

sections.heading: The unity assumption
sections.work: states the thesis and the assumption it denies

sections.heading: Two classes of move
sections.establishes: The phenomena attributed to common ground license two classes of conversational move: what may be presupposed in assertion, which tracks what the participants have publicly settled, and the moves by which they conduct the conversation as a joint activity — designing utterances for one another, judging when a contribution has been understood, insinuating — which track what they mutually represent whether or not it is settled.
sections.refuted_by: Both classes of move answer to the same conditions, so the division marks no difference in what licenses them.
sections.address: Stalnaker's claim in 'Common Ground' (2002) that the phenomena are explained by mutual acceptance of a single conversational state, which licenses assertion and coordination alike.

takes_as_given.claim: Both patterns are standardly attributed to a single phenomenon called common ground.

sections.work: the division every later section takes up

sections.heading: The publicity differential
sections.establishes: Presupposition-licensing is sensitive to public accessibility in a way that coordination is not: assertion fails when a presupposition lacks public standing even where the speaker correctly believes the hearer shares the relevant mental state.
sections.refuted_by: Coordination requires public standing in the same way and to the same degree as presupposition-licensing.
sections.address: Yalcin's account in 'Defining common ground' (2024), on which common ground is common knowledge that p is accepted — a single publicity condition governing every use of it.

takes_as_given.claim: The phenomena attributed to common ground license two classes of conversational move: what may be presupposed in assertion, which tracks what the participants have publicly settled, and the moves by which they conduct the conversation as a joint activity — designing utterances for one another, judging when a contribution has been understood, insinuating — which track what they mutually represent whether or not it is settled.
Publicity conditions are diagnostic of normative rather than psychological structure.

sections.work: the first half of the inversion: presupposition requires public standing

sections.heading: What mutual representation governs
sections.establishes: The mutual-representation mechanism governs conversation as a coordinated activity — how utterances are designed for a particular hearer, when a contribution counts as understood, what may be left implicit — and insinuation is its diagnostic case, because insinuation is felicitous only if the content is mutually recognised AND not publicly settled.
sections.refuted_by: Insinuated content enters the common ground in the way asserted content does, so licensing it requires no second mechanism.
sections.address: Elisabeth Camp, 'Insinuation, Common Ground, and the Conversational Record', on which insinuation communicates content 'without adding it to the conversational record, or sometimes even to the common ground' — a taxonomy of further bodies of information within one system, where this thesis posits two mechanisms.

takes_as_given.claim: The phenomena attributed to common ground license two classes of conversational move: what may be presupposed in assertion, which tracks what the participants have publicly settled, and the moves by which they conduct the conversation as a joint activity — designing utterances for one another, judging when a contribution has been understood, insinuating — which track what they mutually represent whether or not it is settled.
Conversation is itself a joint activity, whose conduct requires participants to represent one another's states.
Insinuation is felicitous only where the audience recovers the content, and is defeated by being put explicitly on the record.

sections.work: keeps the thesis a claim about pragmatics rather than about the difference between talking and acting together; insinuation isolates the mechanism because it is the one move whose felicity requires the absence of public settlement, so it is diagnostic rather than exhaustive

sections.heading: Repair, and its absence
sections.establishes: Presupposition failure is repaired retroactively by accommodation, which alters what is publicly settled, whereas a missed insinuation admits no repair at all: any move that would publicly repair it settles the content and so destroys the move being repaired, leaving the speaker only to update their representation of the hearer.
sections.refuted_by: Insinuation has a repair procedure of its own, or presupposition failure can be met without altering what is publicly settled.
sections.address: Clark and Brennan's grounding account ('Grounding in Communication', 1991), on which one process — grounding — establishes and repairs common ground, and on which 'all collective actions are built on common ground and its accumulation', so every communicative failure is met by the same repair.

sections.work: the second half of the case: the two mechanisms differ in failure conditions as well as success conditions, and the asymmetry is derived rather than observed

sections.heading: Transition
sections.establishes: One and the same content changes what it licenses as it moves onto the public record — by assertion, by entailment from what is asserted, or by the hearer's uptake — ceasing to support insinuation and beginning to license presupposition, while what the participants mutually represent stays as it was.
sections.refuted_by: What content licenses does not change when it moves onto the record, or the move is accompanied by a change in what participants mutually represent that explains the difference on its own.
sections.address: Yalcin, 'Defining common ground' (2024): p is common ground iff it is common knowledge that p is accepted — so becoming publicly settled just is a change in a mutual attitude, and there is no transition between tracks to observe.

sections.heading: Independence without coincidence
sections.establishes: The two mechanisms operate independently — neither is defined in terms of the other, and each functions where the other is absent — while their outputs converge in ordinary cooperative talk because both respond to the same communicative inputs.
sections.refuted_by: One mechanism is defined in terms of the other, or both are aspects of a single state accessed in two ways.

sections.heading: The cost of unification
sections.establishes: Any account treating common ground as a single mechanism must either leave one of the two differentials unexplained or recover it by adding structure that does no other work.
sections.refuted_by: A single-mechanism account explains both differentials without adding structure that does no other work.

outlines.load_bearing: Presupposition-licensing is sensitive to public accessibility in a way that coordination is not: assertion fails when a presupposition lacks public standing even where the speaker correctly believes the hearer shares the relevant mental state.

gap.statement: The two differentials must be best explained by independent mechanisms rather than by one mechanism with two modes of access; this requires that no single-state account can generate a publicity asymmetry and a repair asymmetry together without structure introduced solely to produce them.

outlines.surprise: The two mechanisms are shown to make opposite demands on the same content rather than merely different ones: presupposition needs public settlement, insinuation needs its absence, and deniability is the gap between them. The convergence is then explained rather than left brute — both answer to the same communicative inputs — which is what earns the word 'accidental' instead of asserting it.
outlines.commitment: It denies that the differentials can be absorbed as performance effects or context-sensitivity — the two must be structural. A cautious version would claim only that the phenomena are theoretically distinct while drawing on one resource; this one denies the shared resource.
